We focus on developing real-world applications using neural interfaces while exploring the vital intersections of neuroscience, neural engineering, and neuroethics. By providing accessible hardware resources and fostering a collaborative community, we empower students to transform their ideas into impactful innovations. We're open to everyone, from all majors!

clubs.name: Taiko Kai

clubs.description: Taiko Kai’s purpose is to celebrate and share the traditional Japanese performing art of taiko drumming across all communities by educating each other on the artform and cultural significance. UW students can join regardless of experience or background; we aim to nurture everyone's curiosity about taiko. Taiko Kai offers holistic development through providing a variety of opportunities for members to be involved: typical practices for honing drumming techniques, the maintenance and care of our equipment, creative work such as uniform-making and designing promotional material, and experiencing the range of venues and organizations that invite us to perform for them. Through our efforts to bring taiko to all audiences while providing the space for members to contribute how they want to, we've cultivated a space that upholds our values of inclusivity and empowerment.

clubs.name: Woof3D

clubs.description: As the 3D printing club at UW, we provide a hub for anyone interested in 3D printing. Whether you're a beginner or an expert, we have something for everyone. Experience is not required, and neither is any time commitment. During Fall Quarter, we hold weekly workshops mostly aimed towards beginners. These will teach the basics of 3D modeling in OnShape, as well as how to print using the club printers. We also provide members with the opportunity to work on a larger scale 3D printing project with other members throughout the year. Joining a team is not required, but it is a good way to get hands on experience and learn more about hardware and software in the process. Check out our website to learn more!
